=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clear paired leaves at each node visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped near the apex, with no long internodes visible)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade, not divided into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): obtuse (rounded tip, not sharply pointed)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly rounded, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein with lateral veins branching off and running parallel to margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced widely, 3–5 pairs per leaf (clearly visible in close-up images, especially on upper surface)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy and reflective, especially on upper surface)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, less than 1/3 the length of the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round, cylindrical petiole with no wings or grooves)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm, slightly ridged, and brownish, typical of young woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: brownish-green (stem is greenish-brown, with some darker patches)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem surface has slight longitudinal ridges, not smooth or lenticellate)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; not applicable as leaf complexity is simple)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)

F. Notes: Several leaves show small holes and minor damage, likely from mechanical or biotic causes, but no clear signs of insect activity or pathogen symptoms. The seedling is marked with a pink tag, suggesting it is part of a monitoring or research plot. The surrounding environment includes leaf litter and tree bases, consistent with a forest floor setting, but habitat is not explicitly assessed per rules.
